## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

# 🤯 OMG — Oh My GitHub ### 🚀 One Prompt In. A Full Game or App Out. 🚀 [![Status](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-🔥%20works-brightgreen?style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/actions) [![GitHub Issues](https://img.shields.io/github/issues/denaidark/OhMyGithub?style=for-the-badge&logo=github)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/issues) [![GitHub Actions](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub%20Actions-automated-2088FF?style=for-the-badge&logo=githubactions&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/actions) [![OpenCode](https://img.shields.io/badge/powered%20by-OpenCode-111111?style=for-the-badge)](https://opencode.ai/) ```text ╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗ ║ DESCRIBE IT → BUILD IT → TEST IT → PLAY IT ║ ║ ║ ║ One GitHub issue. One prompt. A complete project. ║ ╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝ ``` **No API keys to configure. No server to maintain. No local setup maze.**
--- ## 🤯 What Is OMG? > **Your GitHub issue becomes the product brief.** OMG (Oh My GitHub) is an automated GitHub Actions workflow for creating complete browser games and app projects from one natural-language prompt. Write what you want in an issue and add the `OpenCode` label. OpenCode checks out the project, uses the shared skills, builds the experience, runs tests, verifies the result, and publishes an immutable OmGithub project link from the finished commit. Yes, it creates the code. Yes, it runs the verification loop. Yes, it can expose the result in a temporary browser URL. ## 🧠 TL;DR 1. Open a GitHub issue. 2. Describe the game or app you want. 3. Add the `OpenCode` label to the issue. 4. Let GitHub Actions build, test, verify, and propose the result. ```text Your idea → GitHub issue → OpenCode → tests → immutable OmGithub project ``` ## ⚡ Quick Start Create an issue in your repository with a concrete request: ```text Build a neon asteroid game. Requirements: - Arrow-key movement - Score and restart button - Win and lose states - Responsive browser layout - Run tests and verify it in a browser ``` That is the whole user-facing workflow. GitHub Actions handles the runner, OpenCode handles implementation, and the workflow handles verification plus the immutable project commit. To run against an existing non-default branch, end the issue title with a `branch: ` directive. The directive selects the checkout and is removed before the issue body is sent to OpenCode: ```sh gh issue create \ --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub \ --title "Custom branch smoke test branch: codex/omgithub-site" \ --body "Build a tiny browser page." \ --label Goal \ --label OpenCode ``` The GitHub App validates the branch before dispatching. If the directive is absent, the repository default branch remains the target. ## 🌍 What Can You Build? | 🎯 Use case | ✨ Example | |---|---| | 🎮 Arcade games | Breakout, Space Invaders, Asteroids, Match-3 | | 🧩 Puzzle games | Word games, logic puzzles, card games | | 🏃 Interactive demos | Physics experiments, simulations, visual toys | | 📊 Dashboards | Filters, charts, status panels, analytics views | | 🛠️ Internal tools | Trackers, generators, small workflow apps | | 🌐 Landing pages | Product pages, portfolios, interactive showcases | | 🧪 Prototypes | Turn a product idea into a runnable proof of concept | | 📱 Browser apps | Responsive tools that work on desktop and mobile | ## 🧰 What Happens Automatically? > **The workflow is the product.** - 📥 Checks out your repository and the shared OpenCode skills. - 🏷️ Synchronizes `model/*` and `skill/*` labels. - 🧭 Reads issue labels to select the model and requested skills. - 🤖 Runs OpenCode against the current project. - 🧪 Runs a second verification prompt after implementation. - 🌐 Starts the app and checks the local runtime. - 🔗 Creates a temporary public preview URL when verification passes. - 🔀 Creates and pushes an `opencode/` branch. - 🕹️ Adds an `Open Project` link backed by the repository path, with full-commit links retained for compatibility. - 💬 Posts progress and access details back to the issue. - 🧹 Cleans up temporary tunnels and runner processes. ## 🏷️ Model and Skill Labels Labels let you control the workflow without editing YAML. ```text model/opencode/deepseek-v4.1-flash-free skill/load-sketchfab-threejs skill/gauntlet-loop ``` The workflow validates the selected labels, passes them into OpenCode, and records the resolved model and skills in the run logs. Shared skills are discovered from: ```text .agents/skills//SKILL.md ``` ## 🔄 OpenCode Workflow ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Trigger] --> B[Prepare project] B --> C[Run build.md] C --> D[Run verify.md] D --> E{Public app works?} E -- No --> F[Run public-app-fix.md] F --> E E -- Yes --> G[Run completion-report.md] G --> H{Screenshots exist?} H -- No --> I[Run screenshot-evidence.md] I --> H H -- Yes --> J[Commit and push] J --> K[Create immutable project link] K --> L[Publish report] L --> M[Complete] ``` ## 🏗️ Architecture ```text ┌──────────────┐ ┌─────────────────┐ ┌──────────────┐ │ GitHub issue │ ──▶ │ GitHub Actions │ ──▶ │ OpenCode │ │ + issue text │ │ runner + labels │ │ + .agents │ └──────────────┘ └─────────────────┘ └──────┬───────┘ │ ┌─────────────────────┼─────────────────────┐ ▼ ▼ ▼ Build code Run tests Verify app │ │ │ └─────────────────────┼─────────────────────┘ ▼ ┌────────────────────────┐ │ Commit store + preview │ └────────────────────────┘ ``` ## 🔐 Security and Access - 🔑 You do not need to create or store a project-specific AI API key. - 🖥️ You do not need to operate a dedicated build server. - ☁️ Execution happens in GitHub Actions. - 🔒 Temporary SSH and preview access exists only for the workflow run. - 👀 Review the generated commit before integrating it. - 🛡️ Restrict who can apply the `OpenCode` label in repositories that accept public issues. > “No servers needed” means no servers for you to provision or maintain. The workflow still uses GitHub-hosted Actions infrastructure and temporary workflow services. ## 📁 Project Structure ```text 📦 OMG ├─ .github/workflows/opencode.yml # 🤖 Main issue-to-project workflow ├─ wiki/opencode.md # 📖 Workflow and session notes ├─ wiki/testing.md # 🧪 Verification guidance └─ AGENTS.md # 🧭 Repository instructions ``` ## 🧪 Local Validation Validate the workflow definition before pushing changes: ```sh actionlint .github/workflows/opencode.yml git diff --check ``` ## 🐛 Troubleshooting | Problem | What to check | |---|---| | The workflow did not start | Confirm the `OpenCode` label is applied to the issue. | | A skill was not selected | Add a matching `skill/` label. | | The app URL is missing | Check the local app verification step and runner log. | | The PR was not created | Confirm OpenCode produced a diff and the workflow reached the PR step. | | The workflow ran unexpectedly | Tighten the trigger condition and trusted-user policy. | ## 🤝 Contributing Ideas, skills, game templates, verification improvements, and workflow fixes are welcome. 1. Open an issue describing the improvement. 2. Add the `OpenCode` label when you want the workflow to prototype it. 3. Review the generated commit and Open Project page carefully. 4. Add tests and runtime proof for workflow changes. ## ⭐ The Pitch The old workflow was: idea → tickets → scaffolding → setup → implementation → debugging → deployment. account-credentials.mjs account-credentials.test.mjs callback-workflow.test.mjs capture-start.mjs capture-start.test.mjs console-credentials.mjs console-credentials.test.mjs default-capture.mjs default-start.mjs deployment-retry.mjs deployment-retry.test.mjs fixtures gh-run-watch-logs.py git-build.mjs git-build.test.mjs github-rate-observer.test.mjs gpu-capture.mjs gpu-capture.test.mjs issue-request-contract.test.mjs issue-request.mjs latest-opencode-version.mjs latest-opencode-version.test.mjs live-files live-files.test.mjs live-preview.mjs live-preview.test.mjs log-response.mjs log-response.test.mjs mac-dns-recovery.mjs mac-dns-recovery.test.mjs opencode-failed-comment.md opencode-final-report.md opencode-prepare.mjs opencode-prepare.test.mjs opencode-reporting.test.mjs opencode-ssh-closed-comment.md opencode-v2-api.mjs opencode-v2-api.test.mjs opencode-v2-proxy.mjs opencode-v2-proxy.test.mjs

import { existsSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync, mkdirSync, statSync } from 'node:fs'
import { resolve, join, extname } from 'node:path'
import { createHash } from 'node:crypto'
import { createServer } from 'node:http'
import { spawn } from 'node:child_process'
import { pathToFileURL } from 'node:url'
import { child } from './session-lifecycle.mjs'
import { livePreviewScript, watchProject } from './live-preview.mjs'

export function projectType(root) {
  if (existsSync(join(root, 'package.json'))) {
    const p = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(root, 'package.json'), 'utf8'))
    if (p.dependencies?.next || p.devDependencies?.next) throw new Error('Unsupported framework: customize start.sh and provide static deployment output.')
    if (p.dependencies?.vite || p.devDependencies?.vite) return 'vite'
    throw new Error('Unsupported package project: customize start.sh and deployment output.')
  }
  if (existsSync(join(root, 'index.html'))) return 'html'
  throw new Error('No generated index.html or supported package project.')
}
export async function start(root = process.cwd()) {
  const type = projectType(root)
  const projectRoot = resolve(root)
  if (type === 'vite') {
    const stampDir = process.env.OPENCODE_WEB_DIR || join(root, 'node_modules', '.cache')
    mkdirSync(stampDir, { recursive: true })
    const stamp = join(stampDir, 'default-dependencies')
    const lock = join(root, 'package-lock.json')
    const hash = createHash('sha256').update(readFileSync(join(root, 'package.json'))).update(existsSync(lock) ? readFileSync(lock) : '').digest('hex')
    let old = ''
    try { old = readFileSync(stamp, 'utf8') } catch {}
    if (old !== hash || !existsSync(join(root, 'node_modules/vite'))) {
      await child('npm', [existsSync(lock) ? 'ci' : 'install', '--no-audit', '--no-fund'], { cwd: root })
      mkdirSync(stampDir, { recursive: true })
      const installedHash = createHash('sha256').update(readFileSync(join(root, 'package.json'))).update(existsSync(lock) ? readFileSync(lock) : '').digest('hex')
      writeFileSync(stamp, installedHash)
    }
    await child(process.execPath, [join(root, 'node_modules/vite/bin/vite.js'), 'build', '--base', './'], { cwd: root })
    root = join(root, 'dist')
  }
  if (!existsSync(join(root, 'index.html'))) throw new Error('Static deployment output must contain index.html.')
  if (process.env.OPENCODE_WEB_DIR) writeFileSync(join(process.env.OPENCODE_WEB_DIR, 'deployment-output.json'), JSON.stringify({ project: projectRoot, directory: resolve(root) }))
  const mime = { '.html':'text/html', '.js':'application/javascript', '.css':'text/css', '.json':'application/json', '.svg':'image/svg+xml', '.png':'image/png', '.jpg':'image/jpeg', '.webp':'image/webp', '.wasm':'application/wasm', '.glb':'model/gltf-binary' }
  const clients = new Set()
  const stopWatching = watchProject(root, () => { for (const client of clients) client.write('event: change\ndata: changed\n\n') })
  const keepAlive = setInterval(() => { for (const client of clients) client.write(': keepalive\n\n') }, 20000)
  const buildWatcher = type === 'vite' ? spawn(process.execPath, [join(projectRoot, 'node_modules/vite/bin/vite.js'), 'build', '--base', './', '--watch'], { cwd: projectRoot, stdio: 'inherit' }) : null
  const server = createServer((req, res) => {
    try {
      const url = new URL(req.url, 'http://localhost')
      if (url.pathname === '/__omgithub/live') {
        res.writeHead(200, { 'Content-Type': 'text/event-stream', 'Cache-Control': 'no-cache', 'X-Accel-Buffering': 'no', Connection: 'keep-alive' })
        res.write(': connected\n\n')
        clients.add(res)
        req.on('close', () => clients.delete(res))
        return
      }
      const path = resolve(root, '.' + decodeURIComponent(url.pathname))
      if (path !== resolve(root) && !path.startsWith(resolve(root) + '/')) { res.writeHead(404); res.end(); return }
      const file = statSync(path).isDirectory() ? join(path, 'index.html') : path
      res.setHeader('Content-Type', mime[extname(file)] || 'application/octet-stream')
      res.setHeader('Cache-Control', url.searchParams.has('omgithub_live') ? 'no-store' : 'no-cache')
      const content = readFileSync(file)
      if (extname(file) === '.html' && url.searchParams.get('omgithub_live') === '1') {
        const html = content.toString()
        res.end(/<\/body\s*>/i.test(html) ? html.replace(/<\/body\s*>/i, `${livePreviewScript}</body>`) : html + livePreviewScript)
      } else res.end(content)
    } catch { res.writeHead(404); res.end('Not found') }
  })
  server.on('close', () => { stopWatching(); clearInterval(keepAlive); buildWatcher?.kill(); for (const client of clients) client.end() })
  server.listen(Number(process.env.PORT || 3000), '0.0.0.0')
  return server
}
if (process.argv[1] && import.meta.url === pathToFileURL(process.argv[1]).href) await start()

# Testing and verification

## Use the preconfigured Linux CLI

Run `scripts/setup-linux-playwright.sh` on an Ubuntu worker to install the pinned
CLI, Chromium, Mesa Vulkan drivers, and a persistent Xvfb display. Let the reusable
workflow run this before publishing SSH access. Use `playwright-cli` from Actions
or a fresh SSH shell; let the wrapper supply DISPLAY and the Linux configuration.
Use `playwright-cli -s=check open <url>`, `eval`, `screenshot`, and `close` without
manual browser flags. Load `.github/templates/linux.md` by default. Select `mac.md` instead when
a `mac` label or `#mac` hashtag is present. Match case insensitively. Recheck the actual screenshot after upgrades.

## Capture the Linux WebGPU triangle

Install Playwright 1.63.0 and its full Chromium browser as below. Install
`mesa-vulkan-drivers`, `vulkan-tools`, and `xvfb` on Ubuntu. Serve
`tests/fixtures/webgpu-triangle.html` over localhost HTTP. Run:

```sh
PLAYWRIGHT_ROOT=/tmp/gpu-runtime xvfb-run -a node scripts/gpu-capture.mjs \
  http://127.0.0.1:8000/webgpu-triangle.html --canvas '#wgpu' \

## Test the `-rc` repository at a selected commit

Use the release-candidate repository when you need to test the workflow against
an older or experimental commit without changing the source repository.

Set the repository and commit variables first:

```sh
repo=denaidark/OhMyGithub-rc
commit=<full-commit-sha>
branch=rc-<short-commit-sha>
```

Create a branch from the exact commit and make it the GitHub default branch:

```sh
git push "https://github.com/$repo.git" "${commit}:refs/heads/$branch"
gh repo edit "$repo" --default-branch "$branch"
gh repo view "$repo" --json defaultBranchRef
```

Keep the existing `main` branch and older test branches. Use a new branch name
for each commit so the tested revision remains clear and recoverable. The
workflow checks out the GitHub default branch when the issue title has no
branch metadata.

Create an SSH test issue with the required labels:

```sh
gh issue create --repo "$repo" \
  --title "Check SSH connectivity on $branch" \
  --body $'# Check SSH connectivity on <branch>\n\nVerify the temporary AgentsWeb SSH session, authentication, tunnel, and remote response. Record concrete evidence without exposing secrets.' \
  --label Goal --label ssh --label OpenCode
```

Create the issue after listener installation to trigger one native `issues` run. The
`Goal` label selects goal mode. The `ssh` label requests an SSH-only check in
the reusable workflow. Verify the issue labels and the selected checkout:

```sh
gh issue view <issue-number> --repo "$repo" --json labels
gh run list --repo "$repo" --workflow opencode.yml --limit 5 \
  --json databaseId,displayTitle,event,status,url,headBranch
```

Confirm `event` is `issues` and `headBranch` is the default branch.
Check preparation outputs for the selected `target_ref` and `target_sha`.

Discover and follow the temporary SSH connection with the repository helper:

```sh
bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id> --repo "$repo"
```

Run the helper while the Actions job is active. It reports no command after the
worker closes the tunnel. If it reports no command at the start, inspect the
run steps and logs before changing the SSH secret. `AGENTSWEB_SSH_ENABLED:
true` proves that GitHub received the public-key secret; it does not prove that
the tunnel or SSH service started.

After testing, restore the normal default branch if required:

```sh
gh repo edit "$repo" --default-branch main
```

Project acceptance testing is live production testing. Manually create a real
GitHub issue with the required labels and prompt, then verify the resulting
issue run, exactly one execution runner/session, and the completed production
outcome. Do not use unit tests as the testing strategy; local checks such as
`actionlint` and `git diff --check` are only static safeguards before the live
test.

For an issue-triggered run with `AGENTSWEB_SSH_PUBLIC_KEY` configured, verify
these checkpoints in order:

1. `Start AgentsWeb SSH session` succeeds.
2. `Post temporary SSH connection command` succeeds.
3. `Verify AgentsWeb SSH availability` succeeds.
4. `Run OpenCode` succeeds.
5. `Mark SSH session closed` and `Clean up AgentsWeb SSH session` succeed.
6. The expected branch and immutable commit exist.

The verification loop must confirm a browser entrypoint before public-app and
Pages checks: either `$PROJECT_DIR/index.html` or `$PROJECT_DIR/dist/index.html`
must exist, and remediation retries must repeat that check. Static root
`index.html` apps are copied to a temporary Pages directory; built
`dist/index.html` apps are published directly.

When `AGENTSWEB_SSH_PUBLIC_KEY` is missing, the SSH session and SSH-based
verification steps must be skipped. OpenCode Web, the Cloudflare session URL,
and the browser-based workflow path must still run; the access comment should
omit SSH instructions and cleanup must not report an SSH session closure.

The AgentsWeb public port must be derived from `GITHUB_RUN_ID`, not
`GITHUB_RUN_NUMBER`. Run numbers restart at `1` for each repository, which made
the first OMG run in every newly installed repository contend for port `32001`
and close during SSH verification. The globally unique run ID spreads those
runs across the broker's `32000-32999` port range.

Validate workflow edits locally with:

```sh
actionlint .github/workflows/opencode.yml .github/workflows/opencode-prepare.yml .github/workflows/opencode-reusable.yml
git diff --check
```

Exercise the production checkpoint, startup, capture, and deployment path. Require a ready deployment with desktop/mobile screenshots. The caller must grant every permission requested by the reusable workflow.
Otherwise GitHub rejects the run at startup before creating a job, even when

For goal support, create an issue with both `Goal` and `OpenCode`. Verify one
native `issues` run, successful preparation, and the Goal invocation. Verify

function createMarket(city) {
 const goods = {};
 GOODS.forEach(g => {
   let factor = city.exports.includes(g.id) ? rand(0.58,0.68) : city.imports.includes(g.id) ? rand(1.32,1.48) : rand(0.92,1.08);
   if(city.id==='aurenne' && imports.includes) factor += .04;
   const price = Math.max(1, Math.round(g.base*factor));
   const stock = Math.round((city.exports.includes ? rand(45,80) : city.imports.includes ? rand(12,35) : rand(25,60)));
   goods[g.id] = {price, stock, baseFactor: factor, stockInitial: stock, trend:0};
 });
}
```

function hashString(value) {
  let hash = 2166136261
  for (let index = 0; index < value.length; index += 1) {
    hash ^= value.charCodeAt(index)
    hash = Math.imul(hash, 16777619)
  }
  return hash >>> 0
}

function mulberry32(seed) {
  let value = seed
  return () => {
    value += 0x6d2b79f5
    let result = value
    result = Math.imul(result ^ (result >>> 15), result | 1)
    result ^= result + Math.imul(result ^ (result >>> 7), result | 61)
    return ((result ^ (result >>> 14)) >>> 0) / 4294967296
  }
}

function ridge(y, amplitude, rng, segments = 7, endY = 302) {

  for (let index = 1; index <= segments; index += 1) {
    const x = Math.round((900 / segments) * index)
    const nextY = Math.round(y + (rng() - 0.5) * amplitude * 2)
    path += ` L${x} ${nextY}`

  return `${path} L900 ${endY} L0 ${endY} Z`
}

export function cityScene(city) {

function roadPath(road) {
  const from = CITY_BY_ID[road.a]
  const to = CITY_BY_ID[road.b]
  const dx = to.x - from.x
  const dy = to.y - from.y
  const length = Math.max(1, Math.hypot(dx, dy))
  const offset = road.curve * Math.min(16, length * 0.11)
  const controlX = (from.x + to.x) / 2 - (dy / length) * offset
  const controlY = (from.y + to.y) / 2 + (dx / length) * offset
  return `M${from.x} ${from.y} Q${controlX.toFixed(1)} ${controlY.toFixed(1)} ${to.x} ${to.y}`
}

export function worldMap({ currentId, selectedId = null, large = false }) {
  const suffix = large ? 'atlas' : 'rail'
  const current = CITY_BY_ID[currentId]
  const nearIds = new Set(
    ROADS.filter((road) => road.a === currentId || road.b === currentId).map((road) =>
      road.a === currentId ? road.b : road.a,
    ),
  )

  const roads = ROADS.map((road) => {
    const touchesCurrent = road.a === currentId || road.b === currentId
    const isSelected = selectedId && (road.a === selectedId || road.b === selectedId) && touchesCurrent
    const klass = isSelected ? 'map-road active' : touchesCurrent ? 'map-road known' : 'map-road'
    return `<path class="${klass}" d="${roadPath(road)}"/>`
  }).join('')

  const cities = CITIES.map((city) => {
    const isCurrent = city.id === currentId
    const isNear = nearIds.has(city.id)
    const classes = ['map-city']
    if (isCurrent) classes.push('current')
    if (isNear) classes.push('near')
    if (city.id === selectedId) classes.push('selected')
    let anchor = 'middle'
    let labelX = 0
    let labelY = 15
    if (city.x < 82) {
      anchor = 'start'
      labelX = 10
      labelY = 12
    } else if (city.x > 518) {
      anchor = 'end'
      labelX = -10
      labelY = 12
    }
    return `
      <g class="${classes.join(' ')}" data-action="${large ? 'atlas-city' : 'map-city'}" data-city="${city.id}" tabindex="0" role="button" aria-label="${city.name}">
        <title>${city.name} — ${city.region}</title>
        ${isCurrent ? '<circle class="city-halo" cx="0" cy="0" r="9"/>' : ''}
        <circle class="city-dot" cx="0" cy="0" r="${isCurrent ? 4.4 : isNear ? 3.5 : 2.7}"/>
        <text x="${labelX}" y="${labelY}" text-anchor="${anchor}">${city.name}</text>
      </g>`.replace('<g class=', `<g transform="translate(${city.x} ${city.y})" class=`)
  }).join('')

  return `
    <svg class="world-map" viewBox="0 0 600 520" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet" role="img" aria-label="Map of the Amber Reach, showing twenty cities and the roads between them">
      <defs>
        <linearGradient id="map-bg-${suffix}" x1="0" y1="0" x2="1" y2="1">
          <stop offset="0" stop-color="#f1e7d0"/>
          <stop offset=".55" stop-color="#eadfc5"/>
          <stop offset="1" stop-color="#e1d2b2"/>
        </linearGradient>
        <pattern id="map-dots-${suffix}" width="17" height="17" patternUnits="userSpaceOnUse">
          <circle cx="1.2" cy="1.2" r=".75" fill="#7f866f" opacity=".22"/>
        </pattern>
        <pattern id="map-hatch-${suffix}" width="7" height="7" patternUnits="userSpaceOnUse" patternTransform="rotate(28)">
          <path d="M0 0v7" stroke="#8b9076" stroke-width=".55" opacity=".13"/>
        </pattern>
        <clipPath id="map-clip-${suffix}">
          <rect width="600" height="520" rx="9"/>
        </clipPath>
      </defs>
      <g clip-path="url(#map-clip-${suffix})">
        <rect width="600" height="520" fill="url(#map-bg-${suffix})"/>
        <rect width="600" height="520" fill="url(#map-dots-${suffix})"/>
        <path d="M0 0h600v520H0z" fill="url(#map-hatch-${suffix})" opacity=".5"/>
        <path d="M126 0c34 70 4 116 45 168 43 54 40 103-3 145-38 36-33 105 8 207" fill="none" stroke="#88a9a2" stroke-width="9" opacity=".38"/>
        <path d="M131 0c31 69 2 112 42 163 42 53 38 100-4 142-37 35-31 102 8 202" fill="none" stroke="#f0e7d2" stroke-width="2.5" opacity=".65"/>
        <path d="M304 520c9-54 32-79 76-94 46-16 68-44 69-91" fill="none" stroke="#88a9a2" stroke-width="4" opacity=".2"/>
        ${mapDecoration()}
        <g>
          ${roads}
        </g>
        <g>
          ${cities}
        </g>
        <g transform="translate(42 472)" fill="none" stroke="#777f67" opacity=".66">
          <circle r="17" stroke-width=".8"/>
          <circle r="12" stroke-width=".55" opacity=".7"/>
          <path d="M0-22V22M-22 0H22" stroke-width=".65"/>
          <path d="M0-15 4.5 0 0 15-4.5 0Z" fill="#a05b3d" stroke="none" opacity=".7"/>
          <text x="0" y="-27" text-anchor="middle" fill="#777f67" stroke="none" font-family="monospace" font-size="7" letter-spacing="1">N</text>
        </g>
        <g transform="translate(508 500)" fill="none" stroke="#7d846b" opacity=".55">
          <path d="M0 0h52M0-3v6M52-3v6" stroke-width=".7"/>
          <text x="0" y="-7" fill="#7d846b" stroke="none" font-family="monospace" font-size="5.5" letter-spacing=".5">20 LEAGUES</text>
        </g>
      </g>
      <rect x=".5" y=".5" width="599" height="519" rx="9" fill="none" stroke="#b3a888" stroke-width="1" opacity=".6"/>
    </svg>`
}

'—' : size let chip = `${side === 'buy' ? 'Buy' : 'Sell'} ${qty || requested}` let small = quote ? `${fmt(quote.total)} c` : side === 'buy' ? 'unavailable' : 'none' let reason = '' if (qty <= 0) { if (side === 'buy') { if (!market || market.stock <= 0) reason = 'Sold out until the next market morning' else if (capacityLeft(state) < good.weight) reason = 'No room left in the caravan' else reason = 'Not enough crowns for a single unit' } else { reason = `No ${good.name.toLowerCase()} in your cargo` } } return ` ` } export function renderMarket(state, ui) { const city = currentCity(state) const weather = currentWeather(state) const weight = cargoWeight(state) const transport = currentTransport(state) const tip = bestMarketTip(state) const waterDisabled = state.cash < 5 || state.thirst >= 99 const foodDisabled = state.cash < 9 || (state.hunger >= 99 && state.health >= 99) const restDisabled = state.cash < 15 || (state.energy >= 99 && state.health >= 99) return `

${esc(city.name)} · market day ${state.day}

Market stalls

Trade size
${[1, 5, 10] .map( (size) => ``, ) .join('')}
Open

${GOODS.map((good) => { const market = currentMarket(state, good.id) const entry = state.cargo[good.id] const isLocal = city.exports.includes(good.id) const isWanted = city.imports.includes(good.id) const delta = Math.round(((market.price - good.base) / good.base) * 100) const fairClass = delta < -7 ? 'cheap' : delta > 7 ? 'dear' : 'fair' const fairLabel = delta < -7 ? `▼ ${Math.abs(delta)}% under fair` : delta > 7 ? `▲ ${delta}% over fair` : '≈ fair price' const tags = [ isLocal ? 'local' : '', isWanted ? 'wanted' : '', ].join('') return `
${icon(good.icon)} ${good.name}${tags} ${good.unit} · ${good.weight} kg · fair ${good.base}c
${market.price}c ${fairLabel}
${market.stock}
${entry ? entry.qty : '—'} ${entry ? `${Math.round(entry.avgCost)}c avg` : 'none'}
${tradeButton(state, good, 'buy', ui.tradeSize)} ${tradeButton(state, good, 'sell', ui.tradeSize)}
` }).join('')}
${serviceButton({ service: 'water', iconName: 'drop', title: 'Fill skins', effect: '+55 thirst', price: 5, disabled: waterDisabled, reason: state.cash < 5 ? 'You cannot afford fresh water' : 'Your waterskin is already full', })} ${serviceButton({ service: 'meal', iconName: 'meal', title: 'Hot meal', effect: '+55 hunger · +6 life', price: 9, disabled: foodDisabled, reason: state.cash < 9 ? 'You cannot afford a meal' : 'You are full and hale', })} ${serviceButton({ service: 'rest', iconName: 'bed', title: 'Bed down', effect: '+70 energy · next day', price: 15, disabled: restDisabled, reason: state.cash < 15 ? 'You cannot afford a bed' : 'You are rested enough', })}
${icon('sparkle')}${esc(tip)} ${weight} / ${transport.capacity} kg · ${weather.label.toLowerCase()}
` } function routeTile(state, route, destination) { const days = routeDays(state, route) const risk = routeRisk(route) const preview = travelPreview(state, route) const transport = currentTransport(state) const wants = destination.imports.map((id) => GOOD_BY_ID[id].name).join(' · ') const sells = destination.exports.map((id) => GOOD_BY_ID[id].name).join(' · ') const waterRisk = preview.thirstAfter < 20 const foodRisk = preview.hungerAfter < 20 const supplyClass = waterRisk || foodRisk ? 'warn' : '' return `

${esc(destination.region)}

${esc(destination.name)}

${esc(destination.epithet)}

${icon(TERRAIN_ICONS[route.terrain] || 'route')}
${icon('route')}${route.distance} leagues ${icon('footsteps')}${days} ${days === 1 ? 'day' : 'days'} ${icon('warn')}${risk.label} ${icon('drop')}${preview.water}
${wants ? `Wants ${wants}` : ''}${sells ? ` · Sells ${sells}` : ''}
${transport.short} · ${preview.food} food · ${preview.energy} energy${supplyClass ? ' · thin supplies' : ''}
` } export function renderRoads(state) { const city = currentCity(state) const weather = currentWeather(state) const routes = roadsFrom(city.id) .map((road) => ({ road, destination: CITY_BY_ID[otherEnd(road, city.id)] })) .sort((a, b) => a.road.distance - b.road.distance) const anyDanger = routes.some(({ road }) => { const preview = travelPreview(state, road) return preview.thirstAfter < 5 || preview.hungerAfter < 5 }) return `

${icon(weather.icon)}${weather.label} · markets drift as you walk

${icon(transport.icon)}
${transport.name} ${isCurrent ? 'yours' : ''}

${transport.desc}

${transport.capacity} kg ${transport.speed} lg/day ${transport.water} water ${transport.food} food
${priceLabel}${transport.cost === 0 ? 'On foot' : `${fmt(transport.cost)}c`}
` } export function renderCaravan(state) { const items = cargoItems(state) const weight = cargoWeight(state) const transport = currentTransport(state) const totalValue = items.reduce((total, item) => { const market = currentMarket(state, item.good.id) return total + (market?.price || item.good.base) * item.qty }, 0) return `

What you carry

${weight} / ${transport.capacity} kg · ${fmt(totalValue)}c at local prices
GoodsQtyWeightAvg paidMarketP / L
${ items.length ? items .map((item) => { const market = currentMarket(state, item.good.id) const difference = (market.price - item.avgCost) * item.qty return `
${icon(item.good.icon)} ${item.good.name}
${item.qty} ${item.weight} kg ${Math.round(item.avgCost)}c ${market.price}c ${difference >= 0 ? '+' : '−'}${fmt(Math.abs(difference))}c
` }) .join('') : '
Nothing but dust and a little loose straw. The market is where fortunes begin.
' }

The caravan yard

Every city keeps a yard. Trade in your current rig at half its price.

${TRANSPORTS.map((transportOption) => stableCard(state, transportOption)).join('')}
` } export function renderAtlas(state, ui) { const city = CITY_BY_ID[ui.atlasCity] || currentCity(state) const current = currentCity(state) const direct = city.id === current.id ? null : roadsFrom(current.id).map((road) => otherEnd(road, current.id)).includes(city.id) const path = direct ? [current.id, city.id] : shortestPath(current.id, city.id) const isCurrent = city.id === current.id const visited = state.visited.includes(city.id) const importNames = city.imports.map((id) => GOOD_BY_ID[id].name).join(', ') const exportNames = city.exports.map((id) => GOOD_BY_ID[id].name).join(', ') return `
${worldMap({ currentId: current.id, selectedId: city.id, large: true })}

${isCurrent ? 'You are here' : direct ? 'One road away' : 'City dossier'}

${esc(city.name)}

${esc(city.region)}

${esc(city.blurb)}

Status${isCurrent ? 'Your caravan' : visited ? 'Visited' : 'Not yet visited'}
Local goods${exportNames || 'No famous export'}
In demand${importNames || 'Nothing in particular'}
Roads${roadsFrom(city.id).length} roads
${ isCurrent ? 'The market is just beyond the square. Choose a road when you are ready to move.' : direct ? `The ${roadsFrom(current.id).find((road) => otherEnd(road, current.id) === city.id).label.toLowerCase()} runs directly from ${current.name}.` : path && path.length > 2 ? `No direct road. The first step is ${CITY_BY_ID[path[1]].name}, then ${path.length - 2} more ${path.length - 2 === 1 ? 'road' : 'roads'} to ${city.name}.` : 'No road connects this city to your caravan.' }
${ direct ? `` : '' }
` }

## Objective
- Build a complete browser-based, text-driven merchant trading game: 20 cities, buy low/sell high, six travel modes (foot, donkey, horse, camel, ox, horse-drawn wagon), trade goods including grains, and health/energy/hunger/thirst bars.

## Requirements
- Text-based trading gameplay across 20 cities.
- Buy low and sell high with dynamic markets.
- Travel on foot, donkey, horse, camel, ox, and horse-drawn wagon.
- Goods include wheat, corn, barley, oats, hay, rice, salt, honey, wool, saffron.
- Bars for life, energy, hunger, thirst.
- Responsive browser layout for desktop and mobile.

## Decisions
- Built a polished static HTML/CSS/JS application with no build step or external assets.
- Theme: “The Salt Road,” a warm parchment/forest-green merchant atlas with illustrated city scenes and an SVG map of “The Amber Reach.”
- Added progression goal: grow 320 crowns into 3,000 net worth, then optionally retire.
- Added town services, dynamic market prices/stock, cargo weight/capacity, trade quantity control (1/5/10/MAX), road events with choices, autosave, sound toggle, help, and restart.
- Uses modular ES files: data, icons, art, engine, views, panels, modals, journey logic, and app controller.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created all game code and UI files.
- Created a temporary local server on port 3002.
- Captured desktop and mobile screenshots with Playwright.
- Start screen renders well on desktop and matches intended visual direction.
- JavaScript syntax checks pass for all files.
- Added `aria-label="Start game"` to the primary button so the runtime screenshot auto-start regex can click it.

### Active
- Visual/gameplay verification is in progress.
- Two 404 resource errors appeared in desktop console; likely missing `favicon.svg`.
- Need to inspect the gameplay screenshot (`/tmp/salt-desktop.png`) and mobile screenshots.
- Need to test trading, travel, modals, events, and rig purchases in the browser.

### Blocked
- `playwright-cli` fails because it expects Chromium `1243`; runtime Playwright `1.64.1` with installed Chromium `1248` works instead.
- Use `/tmp/capture-salt.mjs` with runtime Playwright for screenshots.

## Next Move
1. Create `favicon.svg` to eliminate 404s.
2. Inspect `/tmp/salt-desktop.png`, `/tmp/salt-mobile.png`, and start-screen captures for layout/contrast issues.
3. Fix any visual overflow, clipping, or unreadable map labels.
4. Run Playwright interaction tests: buy, sell, service, switch tabs, travel, event choice, rig purchase.
5. Verify responsive behavior at 1440x900 and 390x844.
6. Update `README.md` with game description and controls.
7. Re-run capture and inspect final screenshots.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: complete app shell and start screen.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/styles.css`: all layout, theme, responsive styles, modals.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/data.js`: goods, 20 cities, roads, transports, weather constants.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/engine.js`: state creation, markets, cargo, trade quotes, travel calculations, persistence.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/views.js`: topbar, merchant/vitals, rig, cargo, hero, mini-map and route sidebar rendering.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/panels.js`: market, roads, caravan/stable, atlas main tabs.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/modals.js`: travel confirmation/results, events outcome, help, restart, retirement.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/journey.js`: travel resolution, road-event generation and choice application, rescue logic.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/app.js`: state controller, render orchestration, event wiring, actions, sound/toast.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/art.js`: procedural city hero illustrations and SVG world map.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/icons.js`: inline SVG icon set.
- `/tmp/capture-salt.mjs`: working Playwright capture script.
- `/tmp/salt-desktop-start.png`: desktop start-screen screenshot.
- `/tmp/salt-mobile-start.png`: mobile start-screen screenshot.

import { createRequire } from 'node:module'

for (const [name,w,h] of [['desktop',1440,900],['wide',1920,1080],['tablet',1024,768],['mobile',390,844],['small',360,640]]) {
  const page = await browser.newPage({ viewport: { width:w, height:h } })
  const errors=[]
  page.on('pageerror', e=>errors.push(e.message))
  page.on('console', m=>{ if(m.type()==='error') errors.push(m.text()) })
  await page.goto('http://localhost:3002/', {waitUntil:'load'})
  await page.getByRole('button',{name:'Start game'}).click()
  await page.waitForTimeout(600)
  const info = await page.evaluate(()=>{
    const r = el => el ? (()=>{const b=el.getBoundingClientRect();return {x:Math.round(b.x),y:Math.round(b.y),w:Math.round(b.width),h:Math.round(b.height),bottom:Math.round(b.bottom),scrollW:el.scrollWidth,scrollH:el.scrollHeight,clientW:el.clientWidth,clientH:el.clientHeight}})() : null
    return {
      body:{sw:document.body.scrollWidth, sh:document.body.scrollHeight,cw:innerWidth,ch:innerHeight},
      topbar:r(document.querySelector('.topbar')),
      workspace:r(document.querySelector('.workspace')),
      hero:r(document.querySelector('.city-hero')),

      railR:r(document.querySelector('.rail-right')),
      mapCard:r(document.querySelector('.map-card')),

      overflowX:[...document.querySelectorAll('*')].filter(el=>el.getBoundingClientRect().right>innerWidth+1).slice(0,8).map(el=>({tag:el.tagName,cls:el.className?.baseVal??el.className,right:Math.round(el.getBoundingClientRect().right),w:Math.round(el.getBoundingClientRect().width)}))
    }
  })
  console.log(name, JSON.stringify(info,null,1), 'errors', errors)
  await page.close()
}
await browser.close()
EOF

# The Salt Road

A text-first merchant trading game set across the twenty cities of the Amber Reach. Buy low where the harvest is heavy, sell dear where the cupboards are bare, and keep your beasts, waterskins, and reputation in good order.

Built as a zero-dependency browser game: plain HTML, CSS, and ES modules. No build step, package manager, or external art is required.

## The wager

Start in Rivermeet with **320 crowns** and a pair of boots. Grow your **net worth to 3,000 crowns** — cash plus the local value of your cargo — to retire with a fortune worth keeping.

## Features

- **20 connected cities**, each with its own exports, imports, market character, and illustrated skyline.
- **10 trade goods**: wheat, corn, barley, oats, hay, rice, salt, honey, wool, and saffron.
- **Six ways to travel**: on foot, donkey, horse, camel, ox, and horse-drawn wagon, each balancing pace, cargo capacity, and daily water/food costs.
- **Living markets** whose prices and stock drift as days pass and roads are travelled.
- **Life, energy, hunger, and thirst** bars. Supplies drain on the road; run dry and your health follows.
- **Road encounters** with meaningful choices: tolls, highwaymen, shrines, stranded travellers, abandoned carts, dust storms, and more.
- **Town services**: fresh water, a hot meal, and a bed for the night.
- **Autosave** after every trade and journey, plus a resumable ledger and a best-fortune record.

## Playing

Open `index.html` through any static web server, or double-click it if your browser permits ES modules from `file://` (a local server is recommended).

```bash
python3 -m http.server 8000
# then visit http://localhost:8000/
```

### Controls

- **Market** — choose a trade size (`1 / 5 / 10 / MAX`), then buy or sell each good. Green `local` goods are cheap here; red `wanted` goods sell high.
- **Roads** — compare distance, days, risk, and supply costs, then set out on a route.
- **Caravan** — review cargo, profit and loss, and trade in your rig at the caravan yard.
- **Atlas** — inspect any city, its specialities, and the roads that connect it. Select a city on the map to plan a route.
- **How to play** — the `?` button opens the merchant’s primer.
- **New game** — start a fresh ledger after confirmation.

## Project layout

| File | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `index.html` | App shell and start screen |
| `styles.css` | Theme, layout, responsive rules, modals |
| `data.js` | Goods, cities, roads, transports, weather |
| `engine.js` | State, markets, cargo, trade quotes, travel math, saves |
| `journey.js` | Travel resolution, road events, rescue logic |
| `views.js` | Merchant card, vitals, rig, cargo, hero, map and route rail |
| `panels.js` | Market, roads, caravan, and atlas panels |
| `modals.js` | Travel, event, help, restart, and retirement dialogs |
| `app.js` | Rendering orchestration, actions, sound, toasts |
| `art.js` | Procedural city illustrations and the SVG world map |
| `icons.js` | Inline SVG icon set |

## Notes

- The game saves to `localStorage` under `saltroad.save.v1`.
- Sound is generated with the Web Audio API and can be muted in the top bar.
- Layout adapts from wide desktop down to a 360 px mobile screen, with bottom navigation on small displays.
